answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards as a digital kernel for identity, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct content. Like yarrow stalks arranged by chance, the verifier requests random segments at each epoch. Much like managing an orchard of distinct trees, the system audits integrity. Probing along the ridge of storage, failures trigger an immediate slash.
